chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Uthman bin Isa, from Musa bin Bikr, from Sulman bin Khalid, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about the weakened ones, so he said: The stupid one in her modest home; the servant to whom you would say: 'Pray' and she would pray, not knowing except what you would tell her. Also, it is the imported (servant) who does not know except what you tell him, and it is the dying old and the small child. They are the weakened ones. As for a man with a strong neck, fond to arguing and quarreling, who deals with buying and selling and whom you are unable to defraud in anything, would you say that he is a weakened? No, and there is no dignity (to him).

key_terms.الْبَهَاءُ: The foolish/stupid one (lacking intellect or understanding)
key_terms.الْجَلِيبُ: The imported person/foreigner (unfamiliar with local customs/law)
key_terms.الْكَبِيرُ الْفَانِي: The dying old person (near death, losing faculties)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفُونَ: The weakened (those lacking full legal capacity due to age, knowledge, or experience)

ai.seo_question: Who qualifies as 'al-mustad'afin' (the weakened) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines *al-mustad'afin* (the weak) through a cognitive lens, emphasizing those lacking independent reasoning or experiential knowledge rather than merely economic poverty. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal accountability (*taklif*) is contingent upon mental capacity and experiential maturity, excluding the 'foolish,' novice servants, foreigners, the dying, and children from full liability. Conversely, an experienced, argumentative merchant is deemed robust in judgment, illustrating that strength of character and trade acumen do not equate to the 'weakness' that warrants special dispensation.

en.basel-kadem: 10.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Uthman bin Isa, from Musa bin Bikr, from Sulayman bin Khalid, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:

I asked him about the weakened ones, so he said: The stupid one in her modest home; the servant to whom you would say: «Pray» and she would pray, not knowing except what you would tell her. Also, it is the imported (servant) who does not know except what you tell him, and it is the dying old and the small child. They are the weakened ones. As for a man with a strong neck, fond to arguing and quarreling, who deals with buying and selling and whom you are unable to defraud in anything, would you say that he is a weakened? No, and there is no dignity (to him).
